note: Scoring change only — the measurement bench (windows, costs, pins) is IDENTICAL to epoch 6, byte-for-byte. Two changes, both to how a measurement is JUDGED. (a) The integrate stage threshold drops 2.0 -> 1.5, matching every other stage. (b) The integration BAR moves from the pooled TRAIN objective to the WORST TRAIN YEAR, because the pooled objective is substantially a 2022 measurement and a merge that trades the 2022 tail for 2023 steadiness could not register under it. No backtest is needed: both are functions of data already stored (ledger columns and data/series/ curves).
changedFromPreviousEpoch: objective.stageThresholds.integrate 2.0 -> 1.5 (the 2.0 bar never bound: 0 of the top-16 rows by objective failed it, and the only 3 rows in the 1.5-2.0 band score objective <= 0.2970)
objective.integrateBar added: basis "worstTrainYear" — an integration candidate must beat the best member on its WORST TRAIN year, not on the pooled window
objective.integrateBar.pooledIsVeto = false — the pooled comparison is reported as evidence and no longer rejects a candidate on its own

comparability.trainResultsFromEarlierEpochs: Fully comparable with epoch 6. Windows, costs and pins are unchanged, so every epoch-6 row remains a current measurement and nothing is re-run. The `epoch` column still records which bench MEASURED a row; objective, gate and the integration bar follow the ACTIVE scoring rule and are recomputed from stored data.
comparability.measurementPreservedNote: Scoring-only change; the measurement bench is identical to epoch 6. Same class of bump as epoch 5.

integrateBar.note: The candidate's worst TRAIN calendar year must beat the best member's worst TRAIN calendar year, on the same (annual - maxDrawdown)/100 metric computed WITHIN each year. A maximin, so the comparison picks whichever member is most consistent rather than whichever earned most. Needs the daily curve of the candidate and of at least one member (data/series/); when a curve is missing the guard falls back to the pooled rule and must SAY SO — a silently relaxed bar is worse than a strict one.

rationale.orderVolumeRatio: Unset, an order can absorb an implausible share of a bar. That is the mechanism behind the two highest-scoring strategies in the library: the ETF-discount study measured sharpe falling 8.44 -> 1.10 as the volume floor rose, because the edge is constructed from the thinnest instruments. At 1,000,000 CNY, 5% of bar volume keeps a position inside what a real book could absorb.
rationale.fundOrderCost: The override patches set_commission, which does not govern type='fund'. 170 held strategies set their own fund costs, so every ETF result was running on the author's numbers rather than the bench's.
rationale.avoidFutureData: A lookahead guard left to the author means 71 of 215 strategies ran without it.
rationale.stockOrderCost: Economically identical to what set_commission(PerTrade(buy=0.0003, sell=0.0013, min=5)) was meant to express: 0.03% each way plus 0.1% stamp duty on the sell. The bench's intent is unchanged; epoch 6 only makes it actually apply. 36 of the affected strategies declared a CHEAPER open_commission than 0.0003, so the existing ledger flatters them.

rationaleForGate.distribution: Across 124 measured strategies the median sharpe is 1.02 and 2.5 is roughly the 88th percentile; 1.5 is the top third (41 of 124).
rationaleForGate.deadFamilies: At 2.5, five of fourteen families (三进兵, 红利低频, 网格, 趋势技术, 套利) had EVERY member disqualified, so objective was -inf for all of them and carried no comparative information — 红利低频's own page records that its study could never report a delta.
rationaleForGate.asAReturnHurdle: At that family's measured volatility and JQ's flat 4% risk-free rate, sharpe 2.5 demanded an annual return of 37.3%; it made 23.4%. The page's conclusion was that the edge exists but does not fit through the gate.
rationaleForGate.epoch4Interaction: Pinning the execution settings moved one measured strategy from sharpe 18.16 to 11.15, so a fixed 2.5 had quietly become stricter than when it was chosen.

rationaleForIntegrateBar.objectiveIsReturn: Measured over the 60 epoch-6 normalized rows: Pearson r(annual%, objective) = 0.9698, and maxDrawdown supplies only 24% of the spread the formula sees (sd 13.7 against 43.6). So "beat the best member's objective" was in practice "earn more than the biggest book in the universe".
rationaleForIntegrateBar.gateNeverBound: Spearman rho(objective, sharpe) = 0.9836 over the same 60 rows, so the two standards never disagreed. 0 of the top-16 rows by objective failed either threshold, and the only 3 rows between 1.5 and 2.0 score objective 0.2139-0.2970 — far below any plausible integration incumbent. A bar that cannot bind on a winner is not protecting anything, so it drops to 1.5 and the real bar becomes the per-year comparison.
rationaleForIntegrateBar.pooledIsARegimeMeasurement: Across the 13 stored epoch-6 TRAIN curves, calendar 2022 supplies a median 62% of total log-growth, and 63-71% for every one of the top 8 by objective (2022 vs 2023 returns run 286/121, 182/52, 157/55, 156/55). TRAIN is 2022-01-01..2023-12-31 and 2022 was the small-cap rally, so the pooled annual return is largely a statement about one regime.
rationaleForIntegrateBar.whatItFixes: Both 2026-10 merge rounds rejected for this reason and said so. The 全A verdict reads "combining relocates WHICH YEAR earns; it does not add" — under a pooled bar that is a rejection, under a worst-year bar it is the question actually being asked. And the 小盘 case (多因子ML x 小市值) is a merge of two implementations of ONE edge, whose expected payoff is robustness; the pooled metric has no channel to express that.
rationaleForIntegrateBar.whyNotPerYearDomination: Requiring the candidate to win in EVERY year lets one member own the bar in one year and another own it in the other, so a candidate can lose to a pair that no single member matches. The maximin compares like with like: the most consistent member against the candidate's own worst year.
